rationale: After the Venturi mask content block, test the key fact that Venturi masks deliver fixed FiO2 regardless of patient's inspiratory flow — a high-yield AS known trap.
After the safety precautions content block, reinforce the critical concept that high-flow oxygen in COPD patients can abolish hypoxic drive and worsen CO2 retention — a major clinical safety point.
After the clinical applications block, test the ability to match device to a scenario — the core applied skill of this SDL.
After the head-tilt chin-lift and jaw-thrust technique block, test the critical distinction that jaw thrust (not head-tilt chin-lift) is required in suspected cervical spine injury.
After the OPA insertion block, test the key sizing principle — an incorrectly sized OPA can cause obstruction rather than relieving it.
After the airway patency monitoring block, test the applied skill of choosing between OPA and NPA when the gag reflex is present — a common clinical decision point.
After the indications for advanced airway management block, test the absolute indications for securing a definitive airway — a foundational knowledge point for AS11.5.

After the key ventilator settings block, reinforce the lung-protective strategy of using 6–8 mL/kg IBW (not actual body weight) for tidal volume — a classic AS trap with major patient safety implications.
After the ABG interpretation and ventilator monitoring block, test the ability to analyse a ventilated patient's ABG and determine the correct ventilator adjustment — a higher-order AS11.6 skill.
